output_json.patch_notes: Root-cause fix at the shared sink AbstractUnArchiver#extractFile (around the SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink call): before creating any symlink, resolve symlinkDestination (relative targets against the canonical parent dir of the entry, absolute targets as-is), normalize lexically (Path#normalize, no filesystem access so dangling targets are still caught), and require the result to start with the canonicalized extraction destination directory; otherwise throw ArchiverException and abort that entry's extraction. Also wrapped Paths.get(symlinkDestination) to convert InvalidPathException (e.g. embedded NUL bytes) into a clean ArchiverException rather than letting it propagate as an unchecked exception. No changes were needed in TarUnArchiver.java or AbstractZipUnArchiver.java since both already funnel symlinkDestination into this one method. Updated SymlinkTest.java: testSymlinkTar/testSymlinkZip now exclude the two fixture entries (symLinkToDirOnTheOutside, symLinkToFileOnTheOutside) whose targets are outside the archived source tree, since extracting them is now correctly rejected; added testSymlinkTarEscapingTargetRejected/testSymlinkZipEscapingTargetRejected which archive just those two entries and assert extract() now throws ArchiverException and the symlink is not created.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change: archives (tar or zip) containing a symlink entry whose target — after resolving relative targets against the symlink's own directory — points outside the extraction destination will now fail extraction with ArchiverException instead of silently creating an escaping (possibly dangling) symlink. This is the intended fix but is a breaking behavior change for any legitimate use case that relied on extracting archives with symlinks pointing outside the destination (e.g. intentionally recreating symlinks to shared/system paths); such use cases were already unsafe and are now blocked, matching the existing containment check style already applied to the symlink's own location. Full `mvn -B clean test` run (323 tests) passes with 0 failures/errors after the change. Absolute-path Windows drive-letter targets are treated as absolute via java.nio.file.Path/File semantics on the runtime OS; behavior on Windows was not separately verified in this container (JDK8/Linux image) but the same Path API is used, so it should apply uniformly.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-22 symlink-target path traversal in plexus-archiver's shared extraction sink. AbstractUnArchiver#extractFile already validated that the symlink's own on-disk *location* (targetFileName) stays inside the extraction destination, but never validated the string that becomes the symlink's *target* (symlinkDestination), which is attacker-controlled data read directly from tar LF_SYMLINK linknames (TarUnArchiver) and zip Info-ZIP unix-symlink fields (AbstractZipUnArchiver). Both call sites funnel into the same extractFile choke point, so a single fix there closes both alert traces. Added a containment check right before SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(): relative symlink targets are resolved against the canonical parent directory of the entry being created and absolute targets are taken as-is, then Path#normalize() (a purely lexical operation, so it also catches dangling/not-yet-existing targets) is used to compute the resolved target, which must start with the canonicalized destination directory or extraction of that entry is rejected with an ArchiverException. The resolution deliberately uses the canonical parent directory of the just-created target (dirF), not the canonical path of targetFileName itself, to avoid a leftover/attacker-planted symlink at that exact location being silently followed during canonicalization. Also hardened against InvalidPathException (e.g. embedded NULs) by converting it into a rejected ArchiverException instead of an uncaught runtime exception. Verified against the supplied tar POV (now throws ArchiverException / non-zero exit instead of exit 0) and confirmed the identical zip source path shares the same sink so it is covered without a separate code change. Updated the pre-existing SymlinkTest fixtures/tests: the happy-path round-trip tests now exclude the two fixture symlinks that were already crafted to point outside the source tree (revealing they had been silently extracting escaping symlinks before this fix), and two new tests assert that tar/zip archives containing those escaping symlinks are now rejected on extraction.
